newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: FOCUS-Volker Stevin net jumps 25 pct.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Volker Stevin net jumps 25 pct.

text.p: Dutch construction group Volker Stevin on Friday announced a 25 percent jump in 1996 profits to 73 million guilders ($38.1 million), above most analysts' forecasts.
Volker Stevin, which plans to merge with rival Kondor Wessels to create Volker Wessels Stevin NV, the Netherlands' second biggest building concern, predicted 1997 earnings would exceed those of 1996.
Earnings per share rose 16 percent to 13.90 guilders last year and the firm said it had posted an average growth in EPS of some 14-15 percent over the last five years.
"Earnings per share should...be higher in 1997," chairman Aad Baardewijk told a news conference.
Baardewijk said the housing construction market was expected to remain good this year and next, but warned that government regulations were a brake on turnover from some infrastructural projects.

Turnover increased by 3.5 percent last year to 2.88 billion guilders. "Turnover grew despite the long winter," Baardewijk said, adding that 84 percent of group turnover was generated in the domestic Dutch market with the rest in Germany, Belgium, Portugal, the United States, Canada and other markets.

The group posted a small loss in Belgium. "Investment by the Belgian government remains minimal," Baardewijk said, adding that construction business in Germany, Britain, Canada and Portugal were reasonably profitable.
Volker Stevin's order book was valued at 2.02 billion guilders at end-1996, 10 percent higher than at end-1995.
The gross profit margin -- measured as a proportion of turnover -- rose to 3.3 percent from 2.8 percent and return on equity (RoE) rose to 18.7 percent from 16.2 percent.
Volker is to increase the dividend to 5.60 guilders per share from 4.80 guilders in 1995.
Volker Stevin said it could not yet tell when the planned merger with Kondor Wessels would be completed, but Baardwijk noted the deal would strengthen his firm's position in Germany.
"We have chosen a partner already present in the German market," he said.
Volker Stevin stock added 0.10 guilders to 200.20 guilders each by 1300 GMT.
Separately Kondor Wessels announced six-month net profits of 15.4 million guilders, up from a previous 13 million. Turnover increased to 629 million guilders from 539 million.
The group also said it expected significant profit growth in the full 1996/97 year. ($ = 1.918 Dutch Guilders)
